scenes.title: The Spices & The Coarse Crush
scenes.text: Great chai isn’t just tea—it’s culinary chemistry. It starts with whole spices: green cardamom, spicy ginger, clove, and cinnamon. Always crush them coarsely. A fine powder turns bitter, but a gentle crush releases pure essential oils.

scenes.title: Water First: The Decoction Phase
scenes.text: Next, water first. Never add milk yet. Boiling spices and bold Assam black tea in pure water extracts rich water-soluble notes and robust color without fat blocking the leaves.

scenes.title: The Milk & Casein Shield
scenes.text: Now, the milk. As whole milk meets the brew, casein proteins bind to sharp tannins, neutralizing harsh bitterness. Meanwhile, milk fat dissolves fat-soluble spice essences, creating a silky, velvety body.

scenes.title: The Double Boil & The Perfect Pour
scenes.text: Bring it to a rolling boil twice to caramelize the sugars and meld every flavor. Strain hot into clay cups. Fragrant, balanced, and soul-warming. That is the art of authentic masala chai.
